Best Family Vacations in Florida

By Priya Anand · May 12, 2026 · Updated August 30, 2026

Florida is, for a lot of families, the first real vacation — and for good reason. It’s one of the few destinations where a toddler, a ten-year-old, and a teenager can all come home saying it was their favorite trip, without anyone having to compromise the whole time.

This guide covers where to base yourselves, what’s actually worth doing with kids, and the handful of things that catch first-time visitors out.

Why families love Florida

Florida solves the hardest part of family travel: it works for every age in the same trip. Toddlers nap on beach afternoons, tweens run themselves ragged at theme parks, and teenagers find enough independence at a resort to stop complaining about being on a family trip.

It's also forgiving to plan. Direct flights from most major US and Canadian cities, no time-zone adjustment for East Coast families, and a genuinely huge range of accommodation at every price point.

Best areas to stay

Orlando

The obvious choice if theme parks are the main event — but pick a resort a little outside the parks themselves for better value and a quieter evening.

Gulf Coast (Naples / Sarasota)

Calmer water, powder-soft sand, and a slower pace — better suited to families prioritizing beach time over parks.

Things kids can do

  • Theme parks in Orlando, sized for every age from toddler to teen
  • Manatee-watching boat tours on the Gulf Coast (best Nov–March)
  • Kennedy Space Center, a genuine hit even with kids who claim not to like museums
  • Beach days with warm, calm water on the Gulf side — easier for younger kids than the Atlantic surf

Travel tips

  • Book theme park tickets and any character dining well ahead — some sell out months out
  • Afternoon storms are a near-daily summer occurrence; plan pool or indoor time for 2–5pm
  • Rental cars are close to essential outside Orlando's resort areas

Frequently asked questions

How many days do you need in Florida with kids?

Seven days is a comfortable minimum if you're splitting time between a theme park area and the beach. If you're staying in one place, five days is plenty.

Is Florida expensive for a family trip?

It can be as budget or as splurge as you want — outside peak theme-park season, mid-range resort rates and off-park dining keep costs reasonable. Theme park tickets are the biggest line item if that's part of your trip.

What's the best age to bring kids to Florida?

There's no bad age. Toddlers do well on the Gulf Coast beaches; theme parks are most rewarding from about age 4 up, once kids can handle height requirements and a full day of walking.
